Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary announced on 13 November 2026 that the newly constructed six-lane Kachchi Dargah-Bidupur Bridge over the Ganga River will be named ‘Nitish Setu’ , after former Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar . Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to inaugurate the bridge on 21 November 2026. Key Points: Naming of the Bridge: The Bihar government has named the Kachchi Dargah-Raghopur-Bidupur six-lane bridge as ‘Nitish Setu’ in recognition of Nitish Kumar's contribution to the state's development. The announcement was made by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on 13 November 2026. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will dedicate the bridge to the nation during his Bihar visit on 21 November 2026. Geographical Connectivity: The bridge has been constructed across the Ganga River , connecting Kachchi Dargah in Patna district with Bidupur in Vaishali district through Raghopur. It will strengthen connectivity between North and South Bihar . It is expected to reduce traffic congestion on the existing Mahatma Gandhi Setu. The main bridge is approximately 9.76 km long , while its total length, including approach roads, is around 19.76 km. Project Background: The foundation stone of the project was laid by Nitish Kumar in August 2015 . The first phase, connecting Kachchi Dargah with Raghopur Diara, was opened to traffic on 23 June 2025 . The project has been developed as a major road infrastructure link for the Patna–Vaishali region. Significance of the Project: Improved connectivity is expected to facilitate movement between Patna and districts of North Bihar. It will support regional economic activities and improve access to markets and public services. It is also expected to provide an alternative route to reduce pressure on existing road bridges across the Ganga. national_raw_news.title: Prataprao Jadhav reviews expansion plans of National Institute of Unani Medicine, calls for timely implementation
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Ayush Prataprao Jadhav on Wednesday chaired the 13th Governing Body meeting of the National Institute of Unani Medicine (NIUM) at Kartavya Bhawan-I in New Delhi, reviewing the institute’s ongoing activities and proposed expansion plans. Emphasising NIUM’s role in advancing Unani education, research and healthcare, Jadhav said the institute currently has 71 students across 10 postgraduate departments. Its proposed expansion includes the introduction of five additional postgraduate departments, 35 more seats and a Department of Integrative and Translational Research. Second campus planned at Ghaziabad The Minister also reviewed plans for NIUM’s second campus at Ghaziabad, near Delhi. The proposed campus will include a 200-bed referral hospital, postgraduate education facilities and research infrastructure. Welcoming the proposal to allocate 24 seats to foreign students within the institute’s existing intake capacity, Jadhav said the initiative would strengthen international academic engagement and reflect the spirit of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam (the world is one family). Minister stresses accountability and public service Outlining his expectations from the institute, Jadhav identified three priorities: timeliness, accountability and service. He called for pending matters to be addressed promptly and directed that clear timelines and responsibilities be assigned to every project to ensure effective implementation. He also emphasised that healthcare services and treatments developed by NIUM should reach all sections of society, particularly the economically disadvantaged. Focus on institutional development During the meeting, NIUM Director Prof. Saiyad Shah Alam welcomed the Union Minister and the Secretary of the Ministry of Ayush. He also presented an overview of the institute’s activities, achievements and proposed initiatives. The meeting was attended by Ayush Secretary Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha; Additional Secretary and Financial Adviser Hoyeeda Abbas; Karnataka Additional Chief Secretary, Department of Finance, Ritesh Kumar Singh; Advisor (Unani), Ministry of Ayush, Dr M.A. Qasmi; President of the Board of Unani, Siddha and Sowa-Rigpa, Prof. Asim Ali Khan; and Director General of the Central Council for Research in Unani Medicine (CCRUM), Dr N. Zaheer Ahmed, among other senior officials. The meeting concluded with an emphasis on strengthening institutional governance, ensuring the effective implementation of approved initiatives and improving coordination among stakeholders to support NIUM’s future development. (PIB)

national_raw_news.title: India, Burkina Faso explore cooperation in traditional medicine, medicinal plant conservation
national_raw_news.content: India and Burkina Faso on Wednesday discussed expanding cooperation in traditional medicine, medicinal plant conservation, Yoga and wellness programmes, with Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Ayush Prataprao Jadhav expressing India’s readiness to share its expertise and support the West African country’s initiatives in the sector. Jadhav held a meeting with a delegation from Burkina Faso led by Roger Baro, Minister and Special Adviser to the President of Burkina Faso, in New Delhi. The delegation is visiting India from November 17 to 25, with a focus on traditional medicine and engagement with Ayush institutions. During the meeting, Jadhav said India attaches considerable importance to its bilateral relations with Burkina Faso and is keen to strengthen the partnership. He noted that both countries have a rich heritage of traditional medicines and indigenous healthcare practices, providing a strong foundation for collaboration. Focus on medicinal plant conservation and research Jadhav said he had learnt that Burkina Faso President Captain Ibrahim Traore had expressed interest in India’s support for the conservation and sustainable development of the country’s traditional medicinal plants. India is willing to share its experience and expertise in herbal medicine standardisation, quality assurance, pharmacopoeial standards and regulatory frameworks, the Minister said. He also welcomed institutional partnerships between Indian Ayush institutions and relevant traditional medicine institutions in Burkina Faso. Highlighting the potential for a flagship bilateral initiative, he proposed an India-Burkina Faso project on the conservation and sustainable development of traditional plants, involving India’s National Medicinal Plants Board and relevant institutions in Burkina Faso. MoU and cooperation in Yoga and wellness The Minister said India is keen to support the promotion of Yoga and Ayush-based wellness programmes in Burkina Faso. The two countries could also explore signing a Memorandum of Understanding between India’s Ministry of Ayush and Burkina Faso’s Ministry of Health to establish an institutional framework for cooperation. He welcomed Burkina Faso’s participation in future World Health Organization (WHO) Global Summits on Traditional Medicine and programmes organised by the WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre in Jamnagar, Gujarat. As an immediate step, Jadhav suggested that both sides identify nodal officers to take the proposals forward and work out specific areas of collaboration. India highlights development partnership and capacity building Reaffirming India’s commitment to South-South Cooperation and its engagement through platforms such as the G20 and BRICS, Jadhav said India supports Burkina Faso in achieving its development goals. He emphasised that India’s development partnership is guided by the needs and priorities identified by the Government of Burkina Faso. He also highlighted India’s contribution to capacity building through training and scholarship programmes, including the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) programme, the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR) and the PCFD course. More than 250 Burkinabe nationals have benefited from these initiatives in recent years. Jadhav also acknowledged the contribution of the Indian community in Burkina Faso to the country’s socio-economic development and expressed India’s expectation of continued support from the Burkinabe government in ensuring the community’s safety and security. He said India remains committed to advancing traditional medicine cooperation through knowledge exchange, institutional collaboration and capacity building, and wished the visiting delegation a productive visit. Senior officials from both sides attend meeting The Burkina Faso delegation included Prof. Rakissida Alfred Ouedraogo, Special Ministerial Advisor for Higher Education and Health Issues; Dr Mariam Sawadogo/Bagayan, Director of Traditional and Alternative Medicine at the Ministry of Health; Prof. Aminata Pagnimdebsom Nacoulma, a pharmacognosy specialist and lecturer-researcher at Joseph Ki-Zerbo University; and Dr Hyacinthe Bonkoungou, Director of the Center for Traditional Medicine and Integrated Care. The Burkina Faso Embassy was represented by Ambassador Some Désiré Boniface, Deputy Chief of Mission Zingué-ouattara Didier Christian and interpreter Ouoba Joël. India’s Ambassador to Burkina Faso O.P. Meena and Kailash Bhatt, Under Secretary (Central and West Africa) in the Ministry of External Affairs, also attended. Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, and senior officials of the Ministry were present. The meeting reaffirmed the shared commitment of India and Burkina Faso to deepen cooperation in traditional medicine and strengthen institutional ties between their respective healthcare and research organisations. (PIB)

The agreement was signed in New Delhi on November 18, 2026, in the presence of Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh under the Other Capital Procurement Procedure. Manipur registers 317 cases under NDPS Act in 2026: NCB official November 19, 2026 Correspondent IMPHAL, NOV 18: As many as 441 persons were arrested as law enforcing agencies in Manipur registered a total of 317 cases during the current year till October compared to 284 NDPS cases with 349 arrests in the previous year 2025, an official of the Narcotic Control Bureau (NCB), Imphal Zonal Unit. The superintendent of NCB added that a total of 269 persons arrested in different NDPS cases were currently in jail and 166 on bail. While sharing the data, Aram Anth, the superintendent of NCB, Imphal Zonal Unit revealed the challenges being faced by law enforcing agencies in dealing with the drug trafficking in the state, particularly cross border trafficking. He was speaking as a resource person at a one-day media workshop (Varta) hosted by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Regional Office, Imphal in Thoubal district today. He said that as Manipur shares an international border with Myanmar, close to the Golden Triangle region, the region faces a persistent drug trafficking challenge. Long borders and difficult terrain made it a challenging task for the law enforcing agencies in dealing with the menace, he said, before adding that lasting results need community support and inter-agency coordination. He said that rampant poppy cultivation practices in the hill region of the state were other challenges in the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan (NMBA), a nationwide campaign launched by the Central government, in the state. citing the impact of the illicit practice on the environment, he said, “Environmental perspective-ecological disaster, soil erosion, landslides, loss of flora and fauna, increases in crime rate, and affect economy/production were the impact of the illicit practice.” Launched on 15 August 2020, the NMBA is a nationwide people’s movement against substance abuse. The main objective of the campaign is building India a drug-free nation ahead of the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision. The PIB, Regional Office, Imphal, organised the one-day media workshop (Varta) for the journalists and media professionals in Thoubal, Kakching and Chandel districts. national_raw_news.title: Beyond the big screen: IFFI 2026 to showcase five films about filmmaking - Mathrubhumi English
national_raw_news.content: IFFI 2026 Introduces 'Films About Films' Section With Five International Movies | Mathrubhumi English Home page » Movies & Music » News » IFFI 2026 Beyond the big screen: IFFI 2026 to showcase five films about filmmaking Published By: Salma Sulthana Last Updated: 19 November 2026, 11:38 AM IST Follow us on Photo: IMDb, PIB What happens behind the camera can sometimes be as fascinating as what unfolds on screen. The struggles of a filmmaker, an actor's relationship with a character, or even a film that never got made can reveal a great deal about the world of cinema. The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) is set to explore these lesser-known stories through a new section titled 'Films About Films'. Making its debut at this year's festival, the section will feature five international films that look at cinema from a different perspective. Rather than focusing only on the stories told through films, the selection takes audiences into the lives, creative journeys and challenges of the people who make them. The initiative is part of IFFI 2026's theme, 'Stories Without Borders'. The festival organisers said the new section was introduced following suggestions from established filmmakers, with the aim of giving greater attention to the art and craft of filmmaking. The five-film selection brings together productions from 10 countries, including the UK, the US, Russia, Georgia, Estonia, Turkey, Switzerland, France, Germany and Italy. From a portrait of a legendary director to the story of a forgotten Hollywood screenplay, the line-up covers different aspects of cinema and its history. David lean's life and legacy The section opens with a documentary on David Lean, the celebrated filmmaker behind classics such as ‘The Bridge on the River Kwai’, ‘Lawrence of Arabia’ and ‘Doctor Zhivago’. Directed by Barnaby Thompson, ‘Maverick: The Epic Adventures of David Lean’ explores the director's career, his ambitious approach to filmmaking and the vision that helped shape some of cinema's most memorable works. The 105-minute English-language documentary also looks beyond his professional achievements to examine the personal difficulties and creative challenges that accompanied his journey. It offers an opportunity to revisit the work of a filmmaker whose influence continues to be felt across generations. A family story from Georgia Moving away from the life of a filmmaker, Raul Geidarov's ‘Sidney Lumet's Birthday’ tells a more personal story about family, childhood and unexpected change. The Russian-language film follows 17-year-old Dato, a Georgian boy who lives with his grandmother. Their quiet existence is shaped by the absence of several family members, until his mother suddenly returns after being away for a long time. Her arrival changes the rhythm of their lives and brings unresolved emotions to the surface. Through Dato's experiences, the film explores family bonds, growing up and the difficulties of holding on to one's humanity during uncertain times. national_raw_news.title: World Heritage Week: ASI monuments to offer free entry on Thursday | Mathrubhumi English
national_raw_news.content: World Heritage Week: ASI monuments to offer free entry on Thursday | Mathrubhumi English Home page » Lifestyle » Travel » World Heritage Week World Heritage Week: ASI monuments to offer free entry on Thursday # PTI Last Updated: 19 November 2026, 09:29 AM IST Follow us on New Delhi: Entry to Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)-protected monuments across the country will be free on Thursday to mark the opening day of World Heritage Week, a senior official said. World Heritage Week is observed every year from November 19-25. "Celebrate India's rich heritage! On 19th November 2026, mark World Heritage Week with FREE ENTRY to all @ASIGoI monuments! Explore our magnificent monuments, discover stories of our glorious past, and experience the timeless legacy of India's cultural heritage," PIB Culture posted on X. The official said the waiver of tickets applies only on November 19 for now. The ASI protects more than 3,800 monuments and sites across the country, of which 143 are ticketed. These include the Taj Mahal in Agra and the Red Fort and Qutub Minar in Delhi. (This story has not been edited by Mathrubhumi and is published from a syndicated feed.)
